react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, mummichog m/z-direct network, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converge on a single dominant biological signal: xenobiotic metabolism. RaMP ORA ranked Reactome pathway REACT:R-HSA-211981 (Xenobiotics) at FDR 0.0072 (fold enrichment 519.6) driven by coumarin, and simultaneously flagged the cytochrome P450 substrate module (REACT:R-HSA-211897, FDR 0.0086) through the same compound. Mummichog confirmed the same signal as its top hit (p=0.0045, rank 0) against the human_mfn network, again mapping coumarin to MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism. MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently recovered hsa00350 (Tyrosine metabolism) as the sole enriched KEGG pathway (p=0.0521), with gentisic acid (2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid) as the sole hit — reflecting the known catabolic route by which coumarin is hydroxylated to gentisic acid. RaMP also picked up iron-handling pathways (R-HSA-917937 Iron uptake and transport; R-HSA-6799990 Metal sequestration by antimicrobial proteins) driven by the ferric/ferrous ion identifier (KEGG:C14819), consistent with Fenton chemistry that potentiates oxidative metabolism of xenobiotics. All seven input InChIKeys resolved to distinct canonical structures (reconcile_inchikey: 7 clusters, zero conflicts), confirming no namespace artefacts. Coumarin is the primary driver compound, hitting in two independent paradigms (RaMP ORA + mummichog). The treatment group therefore shows a coordinated shift in Phase I xenobiotic-processing capacity, with downstream accumulation of the hydroxylated metabolite gentisic acid and perturbation of iron-dependent oxidative stress pathways.
